title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'équation des lacets' programme, i.e. Grothendieck's version of the defining equations of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. An element is a pair (p, ξ) with p = 2γ+1 in Ẑ^* (the 'multiplicateur', Drinfeld's λ) and ξ in π̂_{0,3} = π̂_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}), the analogue of Drinfeld's f. On this page Grothendieck pushes these equations down to the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ)' of Ŝ^+_{0,3}. The prime presumably denotes 'modulo ±1'. In that quotient, π̂_{0,3} maps onto the Γ(2) part, i.e. onto matrices ≡ 1 mod 2.

Step 1 (previous page). With σ_∞ = [[0,−1],[1,0]], conjugation by σ_∞ is the contragredient g ↦ ^t g^{-1}. Hence h_0 σ_∞(h_0) = 1 ⇔ h_0 = ^t h_0. The 'two-cycle / inversion' equation (**) σ_∞(ξ) = l_1^γ ξ^{-1} l_0^γ is rewritten as h_0 σ_∞(h_0) = 1 with h_0 = l_0^{-γ} ξ.

Step 2, formula (92). Write ξ = [[A,B],[C,D]] and l_0^{-γ} = [[1,2γ],[0,1]] (Grothendieck's sign convention). Then h_0 = [[A+2γC, B+2γD],[C,D]]. Symmetry of h_0 gives B + 2γD = C, i.e. C − B = 2γD.

Step 3, formula (93). An auxiliary relation C − B = 1 − D (coming from the parametrization of ξ) turns this into 1 − D = 2γD. That is (2γ+1)D = 1, i.e. pD = 1. So the multiplier is the inverse of the lower-right entry of the image of ξ in SL(2,Ẑ).

Step 4 (sign check). In the quotient by ±1, (**) only says h_0 = ±^t h_0. The minus sign would force the diagonal entries to vanish: D = −D, so 2D = 0 and D = 0 in the torsion-free ring Ẑ. This is impossible because ξ comes from π̂_{0,3}, hence lies in Γ(2), so D ≡ 1 mod 2. Therefore (93) holds unconditionally.

Step 5, formula (94). Using the 'pentagon/triangle' type equation ρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 (with ρ the order-3 automorphism), Grothendieck takes the earlier parametric solution (70): ξ = λ ρ(λ)^{-1}. Here λ lies in GL(2,Ẑ) with det λ = ±1; one may replace λ by λ' π_∞, and in fact λ ≡ 1 mod 2. A started computation of λρ(λ)^{-1} is crossed out.

Continuation (next page). D = δ(c² + cd + d²) for λ = [[a,b],[c,d]], giving p = 1/D. Grothendieck then examines the norm form of Z[ω] mod 3, obtaining p ≡ δ mod 3.

Purpose: show explicitly how the cyclotomic-type multiplier of a GT-like element is recovered from its image in the congruence (Legendre / level-2 elliptic) quotient. Concretely, p^{-1} is a value of the Eisenstein norm form c² + cd + d² (up to sign), linked to the order-3 symmetry ρ.
errors: The transcription writes h_0 = h_0^{-γ}ξ; it should be l_0^{-γ}ξ. With the usual l_0 = [[1,2],[0,1]], l_0^{-γ} would be [[1,−2γ],[0,1]], whereas the page writes +2γ. This is a convention or sign issue to be checked against (44)/(65), which are not visible here.

The auxiliary identity C − B = 1 − D is only written as an underbrace without derivation. On the next page a crossed-out version reads 'B + C = D − 1', which is not the same relation. There is some sign instability in the computation that Grothendieck himself was correcting.
The page writes h_0 σ_0(h_0) where σ_∞ is meant.
Minor ambiguity: the letter ρ is used both for the multiplier (boxed 'ρD = 1', more likely 'pD = 1' as on the next page) and for the order-3 automorphism in ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1}.

ideas.what: Reduction of the GT-type defining equations (two-cycle relation) of (p, ξ) to the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ)/±1, giving the symmetry condition for h_0 = l_0^{-γ}ξ.
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT-hat / Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) in the congruence completion of Γ(2) (Legendre family)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT-hat; Ihara (1985–86) for Galois images through Γ(2) / Legendre curve; Nakamura and others later
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller-tower approach; no such computation is published there

ideas.what: Multiplier recovered as p = 1/D, with D the (2,2)-entry of the SL(2,Ẑ)-image of ξ, and D = δ(c² + cd + d²) via the parametrization ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the cyclotomic character with the 2-dimensional (Tate module of the Legendre elliptic curve) quotient of the Galois action on π_1; determinant/character constraints
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; standard consequence of Weil pairing / det = χ

ideas.what: Solving ρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 by the coboundary form ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} (vanishing of H^1 of Z/3 with a sign twist) inside GL(2,Ẑ).
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian H^1 of a cyclic group / coboundary parametrization of solutions of the hexagon-type relation

missed.claim: This is an explicit, independent (pre-Drinfeld-publication or contemporaneous) computation by Grothendieck of the image of GT-type elements in the level-2 congruence quotient. It expresses the multiplier as the inverse of the Eisenstein norm form value c² + cd + d². It is a historical record of his 'équation des lacets' approach rather than a new theorem.
missed.quote: (93) C−B = 2γD i.e. pD = 1 ... le signe − impliquerait qu'on a D = −D i.e. 2D = 0 donc D = 0, ce qui est impossible
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck was computing concrete congruence-level shadows of GT-hat equations. Mainly of historical interest; the mathematical content follows from known descriptions of the Legendre-family Galois image.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, partly sign-unstable matrix computation in the congruence quotient. It is historically interesting as part of Grothendieck's independent GT-like programme, but its content (the multiplier being determined by the SL2 image) is standard.
transcription_corrections: The boxed relation is likely 'pD = 1' (multiplier p, as on the next page), not 'ρD = 1'.
'Γ'(2)' is possibly just Γ(2) (the image of π̂_{0,3}, ≡ 1 mod 2).
